Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We work modulo \(397\). Since the sequence exists and starts at \(1\), the terms are nonzero residues, so inverses exist.

Let
\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1} \pmod{397}.
\]
From
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]
we get
\[
a_{n+1}\equiv a_n(a_n+1)^{-2}.
\]
Thus
\[
b_{n+1}\equiv a_{n+1}^{-1}\equiv (a_n+1)^2a_n^{-1}
\equiv a_n+2+a_n^{-1}
\equiv b_n+2+b_n^{-1}.
\]
Since \(b_n^{-1}=a_n\),
\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027 \pmod{397}.
\]
Here \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\), and
\[
2\cdot 2027=4054\equiv 84 \pmod{397}.
\]

Given \(a_{2026}=9\),
\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}.
\]
Since \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\pmod{397}\),
\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\pmod{397}.
\]
Then
\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+b_{2026}^{-1}
\equiv 353+2+9=364\pmod{397}.
\]

Therefore,
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84
=279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
